predecessors.name: Buyid dynasty
predecessors.text: Isfahan, governed for the Buyid amirate of Jibal; "Over time, he effectively became independent of Buyid control"

successors.name: Great Seljuk Empire
successors.text: Isfahan, taken after a year-long siege in 1051 or 1052

successors.name: Atabegs of Yazd
successors.text: Yazd and Abarkuh, where Garshasp II was killed at Qatwan in 1141

rulers.name: Ala al-Dawla Muhammad ibn Rustam Dushmanziyar

ledger.x: 1008: Ala al-Dawla Muhammad, a Daylamite general of the Buyid amirate of Jibal, rules Isfahan.
1040: Ala al-Dawla annexes Kermanshah and Dinavar.
1047: the Annazids recapture Kermanshah and Dinavar.
1047: the Seljuks seize Hamadan from Garshasp I.

wars.name: Kakuyid-Buyid war over Hamadan
wars.outcome: The Kakuyids invaded Hamadan against Sama' al-Dawla (1023 or 1024) and took Hulwan from the Annazids; peace and a marriage alliance followed, and a Buyid withdrawal order cost them Hulwan but not Hamadan.

wars.name: Seljuk conquest of Hamadan (1047)
wars.outcome: The Seljuks defeated Garshasp I and seized Hamadan in 1047; he fled to Buyid Khuzestan.

wars.name: Seljuk siege of Isfahan
wars.outcome: After a year-long siege the Seljuks took Isfahan in 1051 or 1052; Faramurz received Yazd and Abarkuh as a fief.

certainty.note: City-based principality (Isfahan, Hamadan, then Yazd and Abarkuh); the page gives no frontiers or area.
